notes.summary: This chapter covers positions in a row or class (ranks from both ends, people in between, minimum totals), comparison chains (taller, heavier, scored more) and seating arrangements in a line or a circle. SSC CGL typically asks 1-3 questions from it.
keyPoints: For one person, Total = left rank + right rank − 1. Rank from the other end = Total − rank + 1.
People between two persons whose ranks are counted from opposite ends (no overlap) = Total − (sum of the two ranks). Example: 40 in a row, A 13th from the left, B 17th from the right → 40 − 30 = 10.
Two people with ranks from opposite ends and k people between them: Total = sum of ranks + k (no overlap) or sum of ranks − k − 2 (overlap). The minimum total is the overlap case.
Class rank with failures or absentees: number passed = rank from top + rank from bottom − 1, then add the failed and absent students.
Comparison chains: write one line from greatest to smallest (D > C > A > B > E) and read off 'tallest', 'second shortest' and so on.
Linear seating: for a person facing North, their left is your left. For a person facing South, their left is your right.
Circular seating facing the centre: a person's left is the next seat clockwise and their right is the next seat anticlockwise. With 6 seats, opposite seats are 3 apart.
The middle person in a row of n people (n odd) is at position (n + 1) ÷ 2 from either end, e.g. 11th in a row of 21.
traps: Counting the person himself when asked how many are to his right or left (14 in a row, 6th from the left → 8 to his right, not 9).
Forgetting the overlap case when the question asks for the minimum number of people.
Treating left and right the same for people facing South or facing the centre.
Leaving out failed or absent students when asked for the total number of students in the class.
notes.examTip: For any arrangement question, draw the row or circle first and place the person with the firmest clue (middle, end, opposite) before using the relative clues.

questions.text: Among five friends A, B, C, D and E, A is taller than B but shorter than C. D is taller than C, and E is the shortest of all. Who is the tallest?
questions.explanation:
A is taller than B but shorter than C: C > A > B.
D is taller than C: D > C > A > B.
E is the shortest: D > C > A > B > E.
So D is the tallest.

questions.text: Five boys P, Q, R, S and T sit in a row facing North. R sits in the middle. P sits at the extreme left end. T sits to the immediate right of P. Q does not sit at the extreme right end. Who sits at the extreme right end?
questions.explanation:
Number the seats 1 to 5 from left to right. R is in the middle (seat 3), P is at the extreme left (seat 1), and T is immediately to P's right (seat 2).
Q and S are left for seats 4 and 5. Q is not at the right end, so Q = 4 and S = 5.
So S sits at the extreme right end.

questions.text: Fourteen people stand in a row facing North. Sunil is 6th from the left end. How many people are standing to his right?
questions.explanation:
People to Sunil's right = total − his position from the left.
14 − 6 = 8.
(9 is his rank from the right end, which counts Sunil himself, so it is a common wrong answer.)

questions.text: Six friends P, Q, R, S, T and U sit around a circular table facing the centre. Q sits to the immediate left of P. R sits opposite P. T sits to the immediate left of R. S is not an immediate neighbour of Q. Who sits to the immediate right of P?
questions.explanation:
When people face the centre, a person's left is the next seat clockwise and their right is the next seat anticlockwise.
Going clockwise from P: Q is next (to P's left), then an empty seat, then R (opposite P), then T (to R's left), then the last empty seat.
The empty seats are between Q and R, and between T and P. S cannot sit next to Q, so S takes the seat between T and P, and U sits between Q and R.
Clockwise order: P, Q, U, R, T, S. The seat anticlockwise of P is S, so S is to the immediate right of P.

questions.text: Seven persons A, B, C, D, E, F and G sit in a row facing North. D sits exactly in the middle. A sits third to the left of D. E sits at the extreme right end. B sits second to the right of A. C is an immediate neighbour of E. G is not an immediate neighbour of A. How many persons sit between F and C?
questions.explanation:
Number the seats 1 to 7 from the left. D = 4 (middle), A = 1 (third to the left of D), E = 7, B = 3 (second to the right of A), C = 6 (next to E).
F and G take seats 2 and 5. G is not next to A, so G = 5 and F = 2.
Order: A F B D G C E.
B, D and G sit between F (seat 2) and C (seat 6), so the answer is 3.

questions.text: In an examination, Kiran ranked 11th from the top and 29th from the bottom among the students who passed. 5 students failed and 3 students did not appear. How many students are there in the class?
questions.explanation:
Students who passed = 11 + 29 − 1 = 39.
Add those who failed and those who were absent: 39 + 5 + 3 = 47.
So there are 47 students in the class.

questions.text: In a test, Amit scored more than Bina but less than Chirag. Dev scored less than Bina. Esha scored more than Chirag. Who scored the third-highest marks?
questions.explanation:
From the first statement: Chirag > Amit > Bina.
Dev < Bina, so Chirag > Amit > Bina > Dev.
Esha > Chirag, so Esha > Chirag > Amit > Bina > Dev.
The third-highest scorer is Amit.

questions.text: In a row of 21 boys facing North, Vijay is exactly in the middle. Raju is 4th to the right of Vijay. What is Raju's position from the right end?
questions.explanation:
The middle of 21 is (21 + 1) ÷ 2 = 11th from either end.
Moving 4 places to the right brings Raju 4 places closer to the right end: 11 − 4 = 7.
So Raju is 7th from the right end (and 15th from the left).

questions.text: In a row of 40 students, A is 13th from the left end and B is 17th from the right end. How many students are there between A and B?
questions.explanation:
B's position from the left = 40 − 17 + 1 = 24.
Students between A (13th) and B (24th) = 24 − 13 − 1 = 10.
Shortcut: 40 − (13 + 17) = 10.

questions.text: In a queue, A is 7th from the front and B is 10th from the back. If there are exactly 3 people between A and B, what is the minimum possible number of people in the queue?
questions.explanation:
Case 1 (A ahead of B, no overlap): total = 7 + 3 + 10 = 20.
Case 2 (B ahead of A, overlap): B stands 4 places ahead of A, i.e. 3rd from the front. B is also 10th from the back, so total = 3 + 10 − 1 = 12.
Shortcut for the overlap case: 7 + 10 − 3 − 2 = 12.
So the minimum possible number of people is 12.

questions.text: Five friends P, Q, R, S and T sit in a row. R sits in the middle and faces North. Q sits to the immediate left of R. T sits second to the right of R. P sits at one of the ends and faces North. Q and S face South, and T faces North. Who sits to the immediate left of S?
questions.explanation:
Number the seats 1 to 5 from your left. R = 3 and faces North, so R's left is your left: Q = 2. Second to R's right is T = 5.
P sits at an end and seat 5 is taken, so P = 1, which leaves S = 4.
S faces South, so S's left is on your right side, i.e. seat 5.
So T sits to the immediate left of S. (R is on S's right, which is the common trap.)
